Earlier: 2026-11-05 (at 7a348e49c, after #267). Real-world cache data is in `cache-real-world-data.md`. Added 2026-11-12: research on paste, drag and drop and `@` context in the chat input ([`research/input-drag-drop-paste-context.md`](./research/input-drag-drop-paste-context.md), rows UX20 to UX32, X22 and X23).

This is the place to check what is done, what is in flight and what comes next. `fork-plan.md` stays as the original design record (why we forked, scope, risks, licensing, CI). Detailed plans for new work live next to this file.

### The critical path

The critical path as of 2026-11-11 (wave 3; states checked with `gh pr view` that day), in the order the pieces unblock each other. It is a reading order, not a promise: the board and the owner decide. What changed since the 2026-11-10 list: the reviewer ran once on a real model and failed its floor gate, so tuning (B34, B35) precedes any further reviewer work; the security review moved the trust fixes to the front; the merge gate exists and branch protection is the owner's to apply; the lab transports are in review and unlock the free local runs; the UI audit became Track UX.

Three things are measured before more is built on them.

1. Free: the false-call scan (RQ7) rerun now that #525 has merged; the false-positive scan of the outbound secret profile over the replies on disk (X6); the Ollama shim contrast on the installed model (RQ16, after MR14).
2. Cents, needs the owner's word: the reviewer on the unified eval set on Nova 2 Lite and Haiku 4.5 (B4) after the tuning in piece 2. The reviewer subtree (the check line in B10, B16, B13, H10, whether Automatic stays experimental) rests on a number that does not yet clear its bar.
3. Needs a Linux run: the escape probes through the sandbox executor (W4c, W7h). Until then every "confined" word is a prediction, and the network half was never run.

### Track C: prompt caching controls

Plan: [`prompt-caching.md`](./prompt-caching.md), [`cache-safeguards.md`](./cache-safeguards.md), [`cache-adaptive-lifetime.md`](./cache-adaptive-lifetime.md) and [`cache-next-features.md`](./cache-next-features.md)

Problem: cached prompts expire after 5 minutes by default, so a session that pauses for a long command or a long read re-reads its whole history at full price. There is no switch for it, no way to choose the lifetime, no cost shown, and two placement bugs mean some sessions do not hit the cache at all. Independent of Tracks A and B.

### Track D: hooks

Plan: [`hooks-wiring.md`](./hooks-wiring.md). Comparison with other tools: [`feature-comparison.md`](./feature-comparison.md)

Problem: the CLI has a complete hooks system (17 events, command and HTTP handlers, Claude Code compatible settings files) that nothing calls, so hook files are read and ignored. Wiring it also needs fail-closed behaviour and a trust check, because project hook files run shell commands.

Status: D1 to D3 are built and merged (#271; they started on branch `feat/hooks-runner-fail-closed`, pushed 2026-11-05, and `hookTrust.ts` and `hooks.failClosed.test.ts` are on main). The trust check has no environment variable, because the CLI loads a `.env` from the working directory. See `hooks-wiring.md`.

### Track G: import settings from other tools

Plan: [`import-from-other-tools.md`](./import-from-other-tools.md). Builds on the Cline and Roo MCP importer ([`import-cline-mcp.md`](./import-cline-mcp.md), #193) and the setup flow (A4).

Problem: people arrive with providers, a model per task and MCP servers already set up in Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Cline or Roo Code, and retype them. The existing importer covers Cline and Roo MCP servers only, and scans for the file as soon as Settings > Tools opens. The import should be a wizard the user starts, with nothing read until a tool is chosen and nothing written until the review screen is confirmed. First scope: providers and model selection, and MCP servers. Rules, permissions and skills come later.

### Track H: policy areas

Plan: [`policy-areas.md`](./policy-areas.md). Research and test notes are in the session notes folder (`policy-areas-review.md`, `policy-areas-prompts.md`, `policy-areas-test-findings.md`, `round2-findings.md`, `research-plan-ask-models.md`: the plan, agent and Loop scenarios on nine models, 60 runs).

Problem: approval is one switch where it should be five dials (Context use, Tool use, File edits, Plan edits, Questions), rules should bind before any level does, the person should decide who answers a question by its type, and a plan turn should hand a reserved or costly choice to the person instead of assuming it. Round one (#356) built the turn texts, decisions, the inbox and the harness guards; the engine, the settings and the remaining gaps follow.

### Track J: context and cost visibility

Plan: [`context-visibility.md`](./context-visibility.md).

Problem: the usage indicator shows how full the window is and what the session cost, not what the prompt is made of, what stayed the same (cacheable), what changed and why, or what could be removed. One day of measurements found tool schemas for servers nobody called, a task list resent up to 107 times, a marker that defeated cross-session caching, dynamic text in the cached prefix, prompts under the cache minimum with nothing said, and totals priced at a fallback rate.

### Track L: codebase index and code intelligence

Plan: [`codebase-index.md`](./codebase-index.md). Research: `research-codebase-index.md` in the session notes folder.

Problem: the index under `~/.continuous/index/` (chunks, FTS5, tree-sitter snippets, LanceDB) is built only when an embeddings model is selected and a `@codebase`-style provider is configured, which a fresh install never has; the agent is never told about it and its two index tools sit behind an experimental flag, so an Agent turn reads the index zero times and searches with ripgrep; the CLI never indexes; JetBrains and the CLI have no type awareness; `core/continueServer/` is a client stub for a hub cache server that never shipped. The published evidence favours a structural index (symbols, references, call edges, the language servers) over dense embeddings for agents, and a commit-keyed index served over MCP as the shape a team can share.

### Track M: which model does what

Plan: the design is in `policy-areas.md` ("The reviewer model") and `docs/reference.mdx`; the handover for the seven `modeModels` entries (`chat`, `plan`, `agent`, `loop`, `replan`, `subagent`, `reviewer`) is in the session notes.

### Track N: Loop parallel waves

Plan: [`loop-mode.md`](./loop-mode.md), section "Next: parallel items as subagents (L4)". P1 (core state), P2 (`core/util/worktree.ts`, #371) and P4 (the IDE workers, #373) are built; this track is what they left open and what the first runs should decide.

Problem: a loop runs one item per turn, so three independent items take three times as long as one, and the research the plan cites says parallel agents are only safe when the harness keeps them off each other's files. The built pieces do that for the IDE: declared `files:`, a worktree per worker, patches merged one at a time. What is not built: the CLI side, anything measured, and the rough edges the first cut chose over scope.

### Track P: command analysis

Plan: [`command-analysis.md`](./command-analysis.md). Builds on the policy areas ([`policy-areas.md`](./policy-areas.md)). Target: 2.6.

Problem: whether a terminal command only reads, writes, or is unknown decides most approvals, and it is decided today by five scanners that read the command as text, all in POSIX syntax, while the shell that runs it is PowerShell on Windows and the login shell elsewhere. A verdict needs the grammar of the shell that will run it, the program told from its subcommand, flags and operands, and a spec of what each does. The first read-only classifier shipped on `next/2.6` and is the starting point; its known gaps are in the plan.

### Track Q: tool-call styles per model family

Plan: [`tool-call-styles.md`](./tool-call-styles.md), the handoff: what is verified against primary sources, what is not, our code today, and the spikes. Started 2026-11-09 from the research on how each family's wire format, tool names and edit format are documented or measured.

Problem: a tool call fails either as text that never parses or as arguments that are wrong for the edit, and both show in our bench runs. Our names and edit format are one set for every family. Vendor documents confirm the wire format and the harnesses Qwen3-Coder was built for, but not the names a model was trained on, so names and edit format are measured before any per-family change.

### Track R: command lint

Plan: [`command-lint.md`](./command-lint.md). Builds on the command analysis in Track P. Target: 2.8.

Problem: the agent writes files through the shell (`cat > f <<EOF`, `echo ... > f`, `python -c "..."`), and quotes, backslashes and `$` are changed on the way, or the heredoc never ends, or the command is bash on a PowerShell host. The shell reports it only after the call has run, or not at all because the command succeeds with the wrong text. A lint before the call can say so and point to the edit tool.

### Track S: stuck detection

Plan: [`stuck-detection.md`](./stuck-detection.md). Builds on the repeated-call guard, Loop mode's stops, M3 escalation and the toolbox drawer. Target: 2.8.

Problem: the only detector is an identical-call counter. An agent that varies a failing command, edits and reverts, re-reads the same files or restates its plan is not caught until a budget runs out, and nothing reads back what it tried or offers a way out.

### Track T: loop budgets and their controls

Plan: [`loop-budgets.md`](./loop-budgets.md). Builds on Loop mode, the usage ledger and the autonomy levels. Target: 2.8.

Problem: a loop stops on a budget, and today the budgets are rounds, tokens and time (the rest are not in the UI). There is no cost budget, nothing shows which limit will fire first, and a limit stops the loop without warning.

### Track U: reviewer isolation and a cached review prefix

Plan: [`reviewer-isolation.md`](./reviewer-isolation.md). Builds on the reviewer role (Track B), prompt caching (Track C) and the review uses in Track M. Target: 2.8.

Problem: a review should not share context with the agent it judges (prompt injection, a reviewer persuaded by the author's reasoning) and should cost little per call. Reviews are already separate stateless requests over a fenced digest, so isolation is largely in place; what is open is whether the reviewer's system prompt and session block are cached, how the prompt is ordered for a stable prefix, and whether provider conversation threads (Bedrock Converse has none; Bedrock Responses, OpenAI and Anthropic's beta do) beat a cached prefix.

### Track V: memory and session history

Plan: [`memory-and-history.md`](./memory-and-history.md). Builds on compaction (Track C), checkpoints and Loop mode. Target: 2.8.

Problem: the model's context is bounded by compaction, but the session in memory, the chat in the DOM and the file on disk are not. Every message, tool output and image stays in Redux, every item is live DOM (no windowing was found in the chat), and a save rewrites the whole session as one JSON. A long agent session or loop can exhaust memory long before the context window is the problem. Nothing shows the person where the memory is going.

### Track W: isolation (WSL, containers, dev containers, sandboxes)

Plan: [`isolation.md`](./isolation.md). Builds on the policy areas (the reserved `sandbox` axis), command analysis and Loop mode. Target: 2.8 for W0 and W1, the rest as measured.

Problem: policy is a guard against accidents, not a sandbox, and commands can only run on the host (or where the VS Code window already is). People would grant an agent far more autonomy if what it can touch were guaranteed, and "run commands in WSL" is wanted on its own. The track starts with an executor abstraction and WSL, then containers and dev containers, an OS sandbox, a jail for whole loop runs with the model key kept outside, network policy, escape tests that generate the claim the UI makes, and the policy axis that uses it.

Invariants for the sandbox axis (design iteration; I3 and I4 there): a sandbox never loosens a lock, a Never rule, a protection or an Ask rule, it only quiets an open action; and **a sandbox prompt-skip never exceeds the File edits level**, because a confined command can still write the workspace and skipping its prompt is an edit nobody reviewed. Without the second rule "confined" quietly makes Editing at Manual a fiction.

### Track MCPW: adding MCP servers (a wizard)

Plan: [`research/mcp-server-wizard.md`](./research/mcp-server-wizard.md) (research of 2026-11-12, recommended defaults pending the owner). **Status: planned. Not in 2.15.0; future release.** Builds on X1 and X1b (pins), the folder-trust path, OAuth sign-in, the importer (#193), Track G, TR3, TR4, TR14, B20, B21, W17 and the PL27 ask-once pattern. Today the add button creates a blank YAML file. A stdio server is a command that runs as the user and a remote one is a prompt-injection surface, so the design never starts anything on paste, shows the exact command, asks once before the first connection, and keeps secrets out of the file. The MVP is MCPW1 to MCPW6.

### Track MR: model and provider research tooling (dev only, never in a release)

Plans in the scratchpad for now: `model-research-tool-plan.md`, `layers-research.md`, `layered-test-strategy.md`. Everything here is dev-only, calls no model unless `--run` is passed, writes nothing to the preset table by itself and commits no data. Boundary rule (design iteration): code that tests our code at a commit stays in this repository; code that measures the world at a date moves to `b1tninja/continuous-lab`. Step one is inside the monorepo: everything that calls a model or the network sits under `bench/` and reaches the product only through one contract module, `core/llm/toolDialects/labContract.ts`, with one integer `LAB_CONTRACT_VERSION`, a pinning test in the product and a golden-vectors file the lab runs at start. Product to lab: pure functions and data only (`classifyToolReply`, `dialectFromChatTemplate`, `verifyProbeCalls`, `recoverFromText`, `coerceToSchema`, the family table and `resolveToolDialectPreset`, `buildReviewMessages`, `parseReviewerReply`, the fixture validator, the shared secret rule set). Lab to product: by pull request only (a generated surface-facts file, new corpus fixtures, a proposed table diff, each with an evidence file); the lab never writes into a product checkout and imports nothing from the product but the contract. Never crosses: raw captures, session-derived text, templates under a model licence, raw OpenRouter dumps, keys. The `bench/lab` scripted suites (MR6) and the capture harness (I23) are step one; the capture harness leaves `core/` in MR7a, its fixture format stays with the corpus.

### Track PL: the provider, engine and API layer

Behaviour is the product of four layers: the model, the provider that hosts it, the engine that serves it and the API surface. The family preset table covers the first. Resolution order, most specific first: the user's own override, a measured result for this exact endpoint, a provider-engine-API preset, the family preset, then native tools with no recovery. Presets only suggest; a leak never turns recovery on by itself. Refinements from the design iteration: resolve per fact, not per record (each fact answers with value, layer, level and date, so a provider preset that knows only "no `tool_choice`" does not hide the family preset's dialect); an evidence floor per action (a warning or suggestion needs a declared or template fact; turning tools off or routing non-streaming needs a declared fact; turning tools on by default needs a measured fact, k of n at the battery minimum, on that surface; turning recovery on by default is never done by a preset, only by the user's override, until RQ7's zero-false-call bar holds for that dialect on replies from that family); a measured endpoint result needs n, a key (provider, host, model, API surface, server fingerprint) and an expiry (a fingerprint change or 30 days), and session counters (Q22) keep k and n live; our own client is a fifth layer, so every measured fact records `clientPath`; a measured fact that contradicts a preset wins and leaves a drift note for the research tooling; staleness is shown, never acted on. The hand-read family table stays "what the template says"; a generated `surfaceFacts.generated.json` (PL1) is "what a surface did, when".

Plans and details: `docs/ci-merge-gate.md`, `docs/supply-chain.md`, `docs/maintaining.md`. Conventions as in the other tracks: one concern per PR, state words are `Built (#N)` only for merged pull requests.

### Track WB: web search and web fetch

Added 2026-11-11 from `research/web-search-and-fetch.md` (merged in #628). Today `search_web` is allowed without permission and is in every tool list; #627 (open) hides it unless the person sets a search endpoint, and WB1 builds the real provider layer. The fork already has the hard parts of a safe fetch (resolve once, pin the address, guard redirects, ask on private targets, an outbound secret profile, a spotlight helper); several are not wired where the data flows. Sizes are S under 2 days and M three to five.

| ID   | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Needs        | State                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| WB2  | Tavily and MCP-adapter backends (a search tool of any MCP server); a key in a URL is rejected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | WB1          | Not started (S)                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| WB3  | Search gate: the outbound secret scan over the query (refuse on a finding), ask on a workspace path or multi-line code, a length cap, one consent card on first use of a backend, a masked audit line, no result persistence                                                                                                                  | WB1, X5      | Not started (M); owner decision (refuse or redact)                                                                                                                                                                   |

### Track SB: sandbox release gate

Added 2026-11-11 from the Windows Sandbox baseline on `main` a049ef0 (harness `D:\temp\sbx-harness`, outside the repository: 28 pass, 5 fail, 2 not applicable). Rule: a release is gated by the sandbox matrix being green on the release candidate (SB1); CI alone is not enough, because CI reported nothing from 20:23Z on 2026-11-11 (CI23) and because the failures below are visible only on a clean Windows machine. Same conventions as the other tracks.

## Suggested next improvements

My own judgement from reading the ten research reports and the code, 2026-11-11. Value is what it buys, effort is S under 2 days, M three to five, L more, and risk is what can go wrong if it is built. It is a reading aid; the Next 20 list and the owner decide.

| #   | Improvement                                                                                      | Rows                    | Value                                                                                                                  | Effort          | Risk                                    |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Make the merge gate real: apply branch protection and find out why Actions stopped               | CI1, CI16, CI23         | Every other safeguard assumes a gate that does not exist; merges since 20:23Z are unchecked                            | S               | low (a rollback command exists)         |
| 2   | Merge the egress fix (#627), cut a release and add `PRIVACY.md` and the release-note sentence    | PV1, PV3, PV7, PV8, WB1 | The product claims it contacts only configured hosts and, until this ships, it does not; an identity and trust problem | S               | low                                     |
| 3   | Model retirement warning and the Anthropic sampling guard                                        | K22, K23, K24           | Two dated breakages (2026-11-30 and a 400 on 4.7+); cheap and testable offline                                         | S               | low                                     |
| 4   | Whitespace probe, server and parser versions in captures                                         | I32, I34, Q52           | Silent corruption of edits for anyone serving Qwen through vLLM; XS effort                                             | XS              | none                                    |
| 5   | MCP client for the 2026-07-28 revision, with `tools/list` pagination                             | O23, TR5                | Servers will move to the stateless form; without it new servers stop working                                           | M               | medium (a spec that just landed)        |
| 6   | Static OAuth client id and scopes, then callback hardening                                       | PL14, PL15, X19         | Unblocks GitHub and Datadog, which have no DCR, and closes the localhost and `iss` gaps                                | M               | low to medium (server quirks)           |
| 7   | Web search as a configured provider, with a gate, fetch limits and URL provenance                | WB1, WB3, WB5, WB6      | Replaces a defect with a feature people can trust; fetch reads a 1 GB body whole today                                 | M               | low (false asks on guessed URLs)        |
| 8   | Reviewer handler for the Nova false allows, then the prompt change                               | B84, B83, B53           | Makes Auto safer with a rule that can only tighten; settles a variance question for cents                              | S               | low                                     |
| 9   | Hook compatibility with Claude Code: `onFailure`, `args`, the missing events                     | D6, D7, D4              | A hook file written for one tool is read differently by the other today                                                | S to M          | low (the `Stop` loop needs a cap)       |
| 10  | The tainted-session rule, replayed on the audit trail first                                      | X17, X4                 | The Rule of Two applied; the biggest unknown in the residual risk list                                                 | M               | medium (friction, measured first)       |

## Later

Carried over from `fork-plan.md` section 4.7, item 4. The four items it listed (checkpoints #185, a global rules toggle per mode #187, context-window and cost display #182, the Cline MCP import #193) have shipped; see the Shipped table. What is left:

- Warn about other costly habits that need Continue's own data first: repeated failed edits in one session, a large model for a small task. The candidates under "Not built" in `cache-safeguards.md` are now rows J2 and J3 of Track J (`context-visibility.md`).
- Per-use reasoning effort, measured: `modeModels.<use>.reasoningEffort` exists, and the turn-prompt eval's act-versus-plan split with the published finding that thinking helps planning constraints and hurts exact-form ones suggests plan and replan turns on reasoning and act and loop turns off for a small model; a K1-style per-family measurement once the mid-task act fixtures (I10) exist, not a default to set from reading.
- Research items without a track yet: variance at n=3 on every prompt change (plan-ask split 2 to 1 on Haiku 4.5; the eval in #361 is where the runs belong); an LLM grader for the plan-ask criteria (decided, assumed, attributed, left as a decision, read the manifest), run on Haiku 5.5 with a human spot-check, since the regex flags misread "the user's choice" as an attribution; a post-plan check that flags an Assumptions line citing the person when no user message contains that choice (the Nova 2 Lite misattribution, caught mechanically); Haiku 5.5 as the plan-mode default candidate (it matched Opus 5.5 on every plan criterion at a thirtieth of the cost, `research-plan-ask-models.md`); the loop packet as the exchange format with projecthub (a plan file with `after:` and `check:` as the one-item contract an arriving agent gets); mid-conversation system messages on Bedrock Converse; a Loop item that asks less on Nova (the Cautious level's agent-answered list is the designed cure); whether the tail reminder helps or costs on strong models, which never see it today (off by default for Agent and Plan on the full profile) until I5 measures it; whether one wording serves every family, or Nova wants the finish-item line on Loop items and Qwen the no-tool-call line (I6); whether a reminder on every user message (#362) or only on the first message of each turn reads better to the model once a conversation is long, measured on the same scenarios with the request dumps.
- More research items from the 2026-11-09 round, none with a track yet:
  - The tail under the `tailored` profile and at n=5: #370 measured `full` and `short`, #366 made `tailored` the Qwen coder default, and both measurements are n=3 (I14).
  - Thinking against tool-calling reliability on small open models: no controlled study turned up (`turn-prompt-eval.md` 6.1 and 6.7); the one Qwen3 ablation on IFEval moves aggregate pass rates by under four points while 10 to 20 percent of prompts flip. Per-family probes before per-family defaults stand (K2).
  - Fewer rules rather than fewer words: instruction following "breaks down beyond 5 to 6 simultaneous constraints" in two 2026 and 2025 benchmarks; the full plan turn carries about twenty rules. Whether the full profile should shed rules rather than words, measured per family with the eval (`turn-prompt-eval.md` 6.3).
  - `toolChoice: any` as a per-family experiment on Nova and Claude only (I12); not portable to Qwen. Whether forced tool choice and thinking can be combined on Claude; OpenAI's rules for tool calling under reasoning effort on Chat Completions, reported by third parties only (`turn-prompt-eval.md` 6.7).
  - A 27B prose comparator for Qwen that is an agent model: Gemma 3 27B on Bedrock used no tool in four runs (`research-qwen-tailoring.md`).
  - Nova Pro's re-plan behaviour (its loop never reached `PresentPlan`), Llama 4 through the non-streaming route (only a direct probe), `qwen.qwen3-vl-235b-a22b`, effort medium and high on Strata, thinking on Bedrock Qwen3-32B, and the "Write not offered" headless evasion case (`research-bedrock-families.md` and `research-qwen-harness.md`, "not measured").
  - Strata's `restores` counter does not count borrows; `requests_reused` and `reused_tokens` do (`research-local-caching.md`). K4 should read those, and the plan-to-act switch's re-read should be recorded on `/metrics` in a real session before the turn text is moved (item 10 there). Server-side Strata settings worth asking for: `--conversation-cache-min-tokens` 1024 to 2048 and 8 slots (slots, not bytes, were the limit).
  - A decision item is not a to-do: Nova Pro gave decision to-dos fake `echo` checks; the first-party Claude models never did. `decisions` on `present_plan` covers it; whether `todo_details` should name the check before `after` (Haiku 4.5 lost its checks when `decisions` arrived) is a three-run question (`research-plan-decisions-live.md` item 7).
  - Haiku 5.5 against Haiku 4.5 on the same scenarios: 5.5 left the reserved choice open 3 of 3 and gave `after` on every dependent to-do at a tenth of the cost (`research-plan-ask-models.md` addendum); the Plan mode default question is in Open decisions.
  - Whether the Bedrock cache counts from the start of a request or its end, and the right factor for `eu.`, `apac.` and `global.` profiles (both in `cache-next-features.md` Open questions, unchanged). Branch scheduling for a fan-out on one cached context (C51, #360): a request sent before an identical one has started its response writes a new entry.

## How to use this file

- Update the "Last updated" line and move rows between sections in the same PR that changes their state.
- Add a PR number only after the PR exists. Do not list planned work as shipped.
- A new plan goes in `plans/<topic>.md` and gets a row under "Next".

- Ids: a row id is its track letter or prefix and a number. The research queue is `RQ1` to `RQ16` (it was `R1` to `R16` until 2026-11-10, and Track R is command lint, so older notes that mean the queue use the same number with the RQ prefix). `MR` is research tooling, `PL` the provider and engine layer, `VA` request-side ageing. Run `node scripts/ci/roadmap-ids.js` after changing ids; a row id belongs under the heading of its own track. Wave 3 (2026-11-11) added `CI` (merge safety, supply chain, release hygiene) and `UX` (the UI audit), and extended the queue to `RQ34` (`RQ19` to `RQ28` from the layered test strategy, `RQ29` to `RQ33` from the grammar review, `RQ34` leave-one-out shedding, which its plan called RQ19), `MR17` and `PL7`.
- Vocabulary for people (proposed, see Open decisions): the words below are what the Permissions page and the docs should say, and the engine keeps its own terms (`floor`, `builtin`, `deny`, `ask`, `allow`, levels, `toolPermissions.auto`). The decision order, in one line: Locks, then Never, then Protections, then Ask, then Always, then who decides.

| Say                        | Means                                                                                                                                             | Engine term                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Permissions                | the page and the whole subject; never "Rules" alone, which is taken by prompt rules                                                               | policy, approval, policy areas                                        |
| Locks                      | always win; no rule, repository, model, sandbox or level turns one into a yes; no switch                                                          | `floor:`, self-protection of the policy files, hidden-command refusal |
| Protections                | a built-in rule you can see and switch off by id; switching one off is a loosening                                                                | `builtin:` ids                                                        |
| Rules (Never, Ask, Always) | a pattern with a decision; Never beats Ask beats Always; only your own settings add Always                                                        | `deny`, `ask`, `allow`                                                |
| Who decides                | for each area, who answers an open action: you, your Always rules else you, a reviewer, the agent                                                 | the five levels                                                       |
| Reviewer                   | the model that decides open actions; "Auto" is not a UI word                                                                                      | Auto mode, `toolPermissions.auto`, the `reviewer` role                |
| Reviewer guidance          | your sentences to the reviewer; never "review prompts", since `continuous review` is code review                                                  | `auto.guidance`                                                       |
| Where commands run         | this machine, WSL, a container or a sandbox; "Sandbox" means only this                                                                            | `terminal.shell`, executor kind                                       |
| Confined (with a date)     | our escape probes passed on this machine for the named properties; otherwise "configured but not verified" or "not confined"                      | `IsolationProperties`                                                 |
| Trusted                    | things you approved by content hash: a folder's config, project hooks, an MCP server's tools and launch command, adopted guidance; one list (B20) | folder trust, `trusted-hooks.json`, `mcp-tool-pins.json`              |
